claims.statement: Organization owners decide whether outside collaborators may request access for unapproved OAuth apps and GitHub Apps. Permission to request is not application approval, installation, data access or bypass of independent policy; pinned product variables identify the two app classes. The linked procedure remains separate review work; no request policy changed.

The Failed invitations view permits retrying or cancelling an invitation through its menu and a corresponding confirmation. The filename refers to expired/deleted invitations, while the text says failed and cancellation; these terms are not silently treated as equivalent histories or deletion semantics. The caption identifies the menu only, not image inspection or a real retry/delivery/cancellation receipt.

Before adding a new team member, the procedure calls for reviewing repositories that the person will gain access to, then confirming the named user/team addition. USERNAME and TEAMNAME are placeholders. The pre-add access review is distinct from merely selecting a user, but no actual repository list, reviewer attestation, inherited-grant audit or added membership was verified.

Organization-level secret creation requires admin access in the containing context. The fragment does not define whether admin means an organization role, token scope or another permission layer; repository admin access must not automatically be generalized to sufficient organization authority. No token scope, secret value, write or credential change was inspected or performed.

The secure-2FA procedure selects both organization-wide required 2FA and secure-methods-only before saving. The conjunction must be preserved, but the fragment does not enumerate secure methods, plan/identity applicability, access loss, migration or recovery safeguards. No actual authentication requirement or compliant membership was verified.

If prompted when requiring secure 2FA, the procedure requires reading how organization-resource access will be affected before confirming. Confirmation is distinct from actual safe enforcement, successful user migration, retained access, a recovery test or blanket change approval; no authentication mutation occurred.
